purpose: Test the pre-registered kill signal against newly observed competitors discussing or shipping post-payment economics.

observations.name: AgentClose
observations.observed: Public product page positions AgentClose as post-payment reconciliation for AI agents. It correlates task/request/payment/delivery/receipt, exposes task cost, tracks retry/attempt lineage, and distinguishes delivered versus exception spend. It explicitly states that it begins after payment and does not choose or approve payments.
not_observed: provider selection using retry-adjusted settled cost

observations.name: SqueezeOS MCP discussion
observations.observed: A public MCP community discussion explicitly defines effective_cost = price × expected_retries, says nominal price can mis-rank providers that fail-and-retry, and states routing priority as reliability then effective cost then latency.

reason: The broad concept of post-payment/retry-aware economics is no longer novel. However, current evidence does not show a credible competitor publishing or routing on comparable exact-task deterministic acceptance plus retry-adjusted observed settled economics across canonically distinct providers, which is the locked kill criterion.
required_claim_change: Do not claim novelty for post-payment reconciliation, task-level cost, retry accounting, or the idea of retry-adjusted effective cost. Restrict differentiation to independently observed exact-task cross-provider outcome evidence that demonstrably changes provider choice and lowers effective cost per acceptable result.
next_gate: Search specifically for a production router that consumes observed post-settlement delivery/acceptance and retry-adjusted settled spend across providers. If found, trigger the pre-registered kill signal; otherwise proceed to the locked provider-choice delta experiment when payment capability is independently available.
